fields.title-post: Prepare your restaurant for the festive season
fields.rt-blog-html:
December is here, and with it comes the holiday rush—whether you love it or dread it. Between the influx of customers, special menus, group reservations, and staff management, everything has to run like clockwork to ensure this season is both profitable and a successful customer experience. 

Here are a few keys to anticipating and making the most of the holiday season.

‍

Why is the holiday season a key time for the restaurant industry?

Before we even get into the numbers and logistics, it’s important to understand why the holiday season is a pivotal time for your business. 

Impact on visitor numbers and sales

November, December, and January are often the busiest months for a restaurant. From corporate dinners to family meals and New Year’s Eve celebrations, there’s no shortage of occasions to gather around a good meal. For you, these are all opportunities to significantly increase your revenue. 

Risks of poor preparation

High foot traffic is great news, but it can quickly become a headache if you don’t plan for it. Out-of-stock items, long wait times, and unavailable dishes—these situations frustrate your customers and put your staff under pressure. What was supposed to be a profitable and festive season then turns into stress and financial losses.

Loyalty and visibility opportunities

The holiday season is a golden opportunity to build customer loyalty and attract new visitors. Meticulous service, an original festive experience or an eye-catching themed menu can turn one-time guests into regulars, and get your establishment talked about on social networks or by word-of-mouth.

👉 To find out more: 2025 marketing calendar: restaurant chestnuts

‍

How should you set up your restaurant for the holidays?

Staffing, supplies and flow in the dining room need to be thought through in advance of the festive season, even before the first order arrives.

Draw up a suitable staff schedule

Developing an appropriate staffing schedule is undoubtedly the first step. Your teams will have to handle busier periods than at other times of the year. 

To deal with them, think about :

  • Plan for occasional reinforcements (extras, seasonal workers),
  • Adjust schedules to balance workloads,
  • Anticipate vacations to avoid unforeseen events.

Plan a meeting with your team as early as November to share your forecasts and allocate tasks. This allows everyone to prepare and avoids unpleasant surprises on the big day.

Manage supplies and limit waste

Special menus, festive products - this season often calls for more expensive ingredients. To avoid food and financial losses:

  • Adjust your orders according to bookings,
  • Choose multi-purpose products (foie gras can be served as a starter and a main course, for example),
  • Keep a close eye on your ratios and stocks via your cash register or management software.

This will enable you to keep control of your margins and reduce surpluses.

Anticipate bookings and attendance

During the holidays, chances are you’ll be swamped with requests from groups. If you don’t have an online reservation system, now is the time to set one up. It will help you avoid “no-shows” and make it easier to plan your services.

This will allow you to adjust your staffing levels, prepare your inventory, and organize the dining area so that every guest enjoys a smooth and pleasant experience. To take it a step further, consider offering pre-set group menus: this simplifies the work in the kitchen while reassuring your guests that their dishes will be available.

👉 Going further: 8 ideas for filling your restaurant

‍

What digital tools can help you successfully manage your restaurant during the holidays?

During the holidays, every second counts, and every mistake can be costly—which is why it’s so important to use the right digital tools.

Software and solutions to optimize organization

A good management tool can make the difference between smooth service and a chaotic evening when customers leave your restaurant with mixed feelings. To avoid this, rely on digital solutions that enable you to : 

  • Monitor inventory in real time,
  • Manage reservations,
  • View team schedules,
  • Analyze your sales.

A connected cash register gives you a comprehensive overview that makes decision-making easier and minimizes unexpected issues.

‍

Personalized marketing and targeted campaigns

The holiday season is also a great time to strengthen your relationship with your customers. How? Here are a few simple ideas:

  • Send out a newsletter with your special menus and offers,
  • Let us know when you're available for corporate meals,
  • Regularly post photos of your festive dishes or room decorations on your social networks.

Also, be sure to create a marketing calendar: for example, a “Christmas menu” promotion in early December, followed by a “New Year’s Eve” promotion in mid-December.

👉 To find out more: Personalized marketing: what's at stake for your restaurant? 

How Can You Increase Your Restaurant's Profitability During the Holidays?

The festive season is often a busy time of year, and a time of spending. But it's important to seize the right opportunities: upsells, special menus and premium customer experiences can boost your profitability. 

Offer special promotions and take advantage of upselling and cross-selling

The holidays are the perfect time to boost your sales with attractive offers: holiday menus, food and wine pairings, and platters to share—but don’t forget about upselling, which can significantly increase your revenue.

This is where upselling and cross-selling come into play:

  • Upsell: Offer a higher-end version of what the customer is ordering—for example, a glass of champagne instead of a standard drink, or a more refined dish.
  • Cross-selling: suggest complementary products, such as a digestif at the end of the meal, a festive dessert to take away or an extra side dish for the main course.

If you have an ordering kiosk, take the opportunity to highlight these options at the time of ordering—in a subtle yet appealing way. 

Optimize the customer experience and enhance your restaurant's appeal

During the holidays, customers are looking above all to enjoy a warm and welcoming experience. The decor, background music, and hospitality are just as important as what’s on their plates. A few small touches can make all the difference: a complimentary hot chocolate for the kids, a house-made digestif for groups, or a personalized note on the table. These details transform a simple meal into a unique experience, and they really make customers want to come back and tell their friends about your restaurant.

Measuring Performance and Preparing for the Post-Holiday Period

Finally, don't forget to take a step back once the season is over. Analyze your numbers:

  • Which dishes were the most popular?
  • What occupancy rate have you achieved?
  • Which upselling efforts were the most effective?

You can use this data to adjust your strategies for the coming year. And why not extend the holiday spirit with a special “galette des Rois” or “January menu” offer? This can help smooth out the post-holiday dip in business.

If there’s one thing you should take away from this article, it’s this: planning ahead is the key to a successful holiday season. With solid, well-thought-out planning, the right digital tools, and a focus on the customer experience, you’ll be able to make the most of this very special time of year.
